notes: The main hand writes from Lodève and addresses Deligne. The day 27 is clear; the obscured month/year is retained as a doubt. There is no identified author page number on this scan. H’s page 3 and its explanatory archive/provenance notes are editorial metadata and are not imported.

The author discusses a possible first-cycle course and a small algebra seminar on the fourbis of Mme Sinh, possibly transferred to the setting of “champs”. The opening cause and one noun remain damaged; faute is the best visible reading of that noun, not a grammatical repair.

The author expressly calls the construction “qui pour l’instant reste heuristique” and introduces the diagram with “il doit y avoir un triangle distingué canonique”. These are author statements, not mathematical conclusions certified by this reader.

The page writes a truncation of a double-stem R followed by underlined Hom, denotes it E(M,N), gives two rows of invariants, and draws a three-object triangle with underlined Hom(M,{}_2N)[-2] at the top. All arrowheads, the prime on E, the lowered left 2, and the shift [-2] were read as ink.

Mathematical details prompting focused ink inspection were the comparison in the truncation, the alphabet of R, the small exponents on both H terms, and the overwritten term preceding Ext. No expected cohomology or triangle property was used to choose a damaged glyph.
No targeted proof, counterexample search, or calculation was performed. The checks list is empty because ordinary symbol reading is not a mathematical verification event.

The separate sideways hand addresses Breen, asks “Qu’en pens-tu.”, closes “Bien à toi”, and signs P. with a surname best read as Deligne. The absent accents in repondre and neamoins/neanmoins are preserved; the shortened pens is not expanded.

The heavy edge lines and isolated vertical registration-like strokes occur outside the text and are recorded as scan artefacts, not as author underlining, a drawing, a cancellation, or a page numeral. The thick line across the date is not assigned an unproven physical cause.

Final validation was syntax-only: balanced TeX braces/environments, required page and diagram macros, JSON structure, all 16 view-log paths, and a one-to-one count of 12 uncertainty macros and 12 residual-doubt records. No LaTeX compilation was run.

coverage: Read the entire 1687 × 2361 sheet once for layout, then upper and lower supplied halves once each, in that order. Every body line, heading, salutation, accent, punctuation mark, mathematical symbol, correction state, complete diagram object/arrow/label, sideways note and signature was inspected against both full witnesses; agreement was not treated as evidence. Thirteen single tight crops address only places left unresolved by those halves, including separately located parts of the long sideways note. No entire half was enlarged again, no decided place was recropped, and no other page, reader output, OCR, web source, or external transcription was consulted. The underlying overwritten word omitted by H is represented with deletion and doubt macros; H’s missing opening words and à la place are represented from ink. A small point after pour, absent in both witnesses, is explicitly doubtful because it may be a reproduction speck. The physical lower-left 61 appears only in an archive comment. No author drawing, insertion, whole-block cancellation, or author page number was identified. The complete page, including every surviving block and the triangle in tikz-cd, is in reading.tex.
